title: AEGS Trust Assessment
description: What is known about a counterparty from prior dealings. Deliberately separate from RiskAssessment: trust is a property of the *relationship*, risk is a property of the *action*, and a familiar counterparty can still be a risky transaction. Cold start must be untrusted rather than neutral -- a new counterparty that scores mid-range is indistinguishable from a mediocre known one.

assessed.description: False means this control exists in the implementation and did not run for this action. Absent from a GovernanceDecision means the implementation does not have the control at all. The two are different statements and must not be collapsed.

score.description: Normalised 0..1, or null when genuinely unknown. Never 0 to mean 'unknown' -- an unmeasured value rendered as zero is not a missing fact, it is a wrong one, and no reader can tell the difference.

indicators.description: Named signals that fired. Absence of indicators is not evidence of absence of risk.

method.description: How the score was produced -- deterministic terms, a model, a third-party service. An auditor needs this to weigh the number.

settledCount.description: Null means not measured. Never 0 to mean unknown -- this exact conflation caused every advisor in this project to treat established counterparties as strangers.

earnedAuthority.description: Any uplift granted on the basis of history. Recording it matters because cheap reputation converted into spending power is a named attack.
